title: One Small Star, One Long Night

shots.caption: A STAR FELL INTO THE DARK.
SHE CAUGHT IT BEFORE IT HIT.
SHE CARRIED IT ABOVE THE STREET.
THEN SOMEONE HELD THE PAPER STILL.
SHE LEFT ONE FOR THE NEXT HAND.
ONE SMALL LIGHT CAN TRAVEL WHEN WE SHARE IT.

creative_intent.logline: In a city where every window is dark, a lone stick figure catches a falling paper star, struggles to keep it intact, then learns to build a string of stars with a stranger. One small light becomes a shared signal that the night is not empty.
creative_intent.hook: A single paper star drops through a dark city. The yellow-wristband figure reaches up and catches it just before it hits the pavement.
hook_candidates: A paper star falls through a dark city; a stick figure catches it before it hits the street.
The only bright thing in the city tears apart in the wind.
A tiny paper star lights one window—and a second window answers.
creative_intent.theme: You do not have to brighten the whole world. One small act can help someone else take the next step.
creative_intent.emotional_turn: The protagonist's solo attempt keeps failing; a blue-scarf stranger steadies the paper, and the final star chain becomes a shared signal across two dark windows.
creative_intent.ending_payoff: The lead leaves one blank sheet by the window for the next person to fold, turning the ending into an invitation rather than a lecture.
creative_intent.character_bible: Lead: white round-headed 2D stick figure, expressive dot eyes and mouth, thin articulated arms and legs, consistent rig and one yellow wristband. Secondary: same white stick-figure construction and scale family, distinguished only by a blue scarf. Both remain 2D articulated stick figures; no anime, photoreal people, or redesign.
creative_intent.prop_bible: A small cream paper star with visible fold creases, a torn version, blank square paper, a short string, a three-star chain, and a dark window that becomes a warm star-lit window. Paper-star props are attached near the lead's active hand; the window prop is staged separately in the city background.
narrative_beats: 0–30s: a paper star falls through a dark city; the lead catches it, but the wind tears it
30–60s: the lead tries to fold and hang a replacement; one point collapses and the string snaps
60–90s: the lead nearly quits, then starts again with a clean sheet
90–120s: a blue-scarf stranger holds the paper steady; they fold a star together
120–150s: they make a second star and connect both with a short string
150–180s: the first window glows; another window answers while most of the street remains dark
180–210s: the lead leaves a blank sheet for the next person; the shared light becomes the final emotional image

candidates.reason: Immediate falling-object hook, clear physical struggle, a meaningful helper entrance, and a visual city-wide payoff; new paper-star prop work adds moderate implementation risk.

candidates.name: The Coat Left in the Rain
candidates.reason: A solitary figure leaves their only warm coat for someone stranded in a storm; strong emotional reversal but requires a new cloth prop and more complex contact.

candidates.name: The Unsent Letter at Dawn
candidates.reason: A character repeatedly rewrites an apology, then chooses a concrete act instead of sending words; intimate but visually less immediate.

creative_intent.description_candidate: A paper star falls into a dark city. One stick figure tries to keep it whole, but the wind keeps pulling it apart. When a stranger lends a steady hand, one small star becomes a light they can share. An original silent 2D stick-figure story about hope, persistence, and the quiet power of helping someone begin again. No dialogue or voiceover.

growth_hypotheses: The falling paper star may make the 0–5s conflict legible without sound; validate using audience retention at 0:05.
The helper's entrance near the middle may reduce the retention dip around 90–110s; validate with the actual retention graph.
The two-window payoff may encourage completion and rewatch; validate average percentage viewed and end-of-video retention.
The final blank sheet may invite comments about a small act of kindness; validate comments and shares per view.

sources.finding: A weekly ranking based on 24 YouTube-returned stick-figure Shorts; current examples include action-led comparison and survival-story formats. Ranking is a directional snapshot, not a verified channel-wide trend census.

Third-party tracker estimates 5.37M views/day for videos matching stickman animation on 11 Nov, versus 2.58M/day on 14 Oct. Treat as a vendor estimate and broad-category demand signal, not official YouTube analytics.
Reports YouTube's statement that microdramas received more than 6.5B views in H1 2026 and that the platform is expanding episodic discovery and monetization.
Reports growth in short episodic drama distribution across YouTube, TikTok and Instagram; supports action-led compact emotional arcs, not a guarantee for this film.

trend_research.interpretation: The current evidence supports testing a simple visual hook and a compact emotional arc. It does not establish that a 210-second horizontal film will go viral.
